high.title: Dragon Capital Forecasts a Series of "Good News" for Vietnam's Stock Market in the Coming Period
high.summary: In its H2 2026 strategy report, Dragon Capital presents a constructively bullish outlook for Vietnamese equities, underpinned by three core catalysts: (1) accelerated public investment and pro-growth fiscal policies, (2) Vietnam's official FTSE Russell upgrade to Secondary Emerging Market status effective September 2026, and (3) attractive current valuations. The firm notes that despite significant external headwinds in H1 2026 — including oil price shocks, Fed monetary tightening, and sustained net foreign selling — Vietnam's economy demonstrated notable resilience, with the VN-Index still posting new all-time highs. GDP growth reached 8.18% in H1 2026, the strongest first-half performance since data collection began in 2011. Disbursed FDI hit USD 13 billion (+11.2% YoY), while newly registered and supplementary FDI commitments reached USD 34.7 billion, signaling robust long-term capital inflow momentum.

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 11: ACB Leads Market at 7.3%/year for 12-Month Term Across MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary:
Vietnamese deposit rates continue to edge higher, with six banks now offering 7.0%/year or above on 12-month term deposits — a benchmark level closely watched as a signal of system-wide liquidity conditions. ACB remains the market leader at 7.3%/year for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2%/year. MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB are all at 7.0%/year, with MBV and VCBNeo extending that rate across 6-, 9-, and 18-month tenors as well. The next tier — Bac A Bank, LPBank, BVBank, and OCB — clusters at 6.9%/year for 12 months, with LPBank standing out at 6.95%/year on 18-month deposits. The state-owned "Big Four" (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) hold steady at 6.8%/year for 12- and 18-month terms and 6.6%/year for 6- and 9-month terms. **Market implications:** The sustained elevation of deposit rates — particularly among joint-stock banks competing aggressively for retail funding — signals persistent tightening in system liquidity. For VND traders, this environment supports VND-positive carry dynamics but may constrain credit growth. Bond investors should monitor whether rising deposit rates feed through to secondary market government bond yield pressure in the short end.

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 12: MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary:
The Vietnamese deposit rate landscape continues to show upward pressure at the private bank tier, with ACB leading the market at 7.3%/year for 12-month tenors, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2%/year. A total of six banks are now offering deposit rates at or above 7%/year for 12-month tenors — including MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB at 7.0%/year — signaling continued competition for retail funding. A second cluster of four banks (Bac A Bank, LPBank, BVBank, and OCB) sits at 6.9%/year for 12-month tenors, with LPBank offering 6.95%/year at 18 months.

Notably, the four state-owned commercial banks — Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, and VietinBank — have kept their deposit rate schedules unchanged, maintaining the policy-aligned floor and acting as a stabilizing anchor. **For VND and bond traders**, the persistent divergence between private and state-owned bank rates signals ongoing liquidity tightness in the private sector. Rising deposit rates, if sustained, will increase bank funding costs, potentially pressuring net interest margins and creating upward yield drift in the short-to-medium government bond curve. Watch for whether state banks follow with any rate adjustments, which would be a stronger systemic signal.

high.title: Agribank Publishes Lending Rate Schedule
high.summary:
Agribank has disclosed its average lending rate schedule for May 2026. Priority sector short-term VND loans (per government and SBV directives) carry a rate of 4.0%/year. Standard short-term lending starts at a minimum of 6.1%/year, while medium-to-long-term loans are floored at 7.8%/year. Credit card lending is set at 15%/year. The bank's average lending rate for May stood at 8.63%/year against an average cost of funds of 7.16%/year, implying a net interest spread of approximately 147 basis points — a relatively thin margin for a state-owned bank of this scale.

**For fixed income and FX traders**, Agribank's cost of funds at 7.16%/year is a key benchmark for the state-owned bank funding floor. The spread between deposit costs and lending rates remains compressed, which may limit the SBV's room to push lending rates lower without squeezing bank profitability. This dynamic is relevant to the transmission effectiveness of any future monetary easing and is worth monitoring alongside SBV policy rate signals.

high.title: Vietcombank Publishes Lending Rate Disclosure — Average Lending Rate Rises to 7.2% in May 2026, Fourth Consecutive Monthly Increase
high.summary:
Vietcombank — Vietnam's largest state-owned commercial bank and a key bellwether for domestic interest rate trends — has disclosed that its average lending rate for May 2026 reached **7.2% per annum**, marking the **fourth consecutive monthly increase**. The spread between average lending and deposit rates widened to **3.5% p.a.**, while the net spread after funding-related costs stood at **2.0% p.a.**

For context, the trajectory has been steep: the average lending rate was 6.4% in February, rose to 6.6% in March, and has continued climbing through April and May. This sustained upward movement in lending rates at the system's flagship bank signals a broader tightening of credit conditions in the Vietnamese economy, even in the absence of explicit SBV policy rate hikes.

medium.title: Dividend Record Date Schedule July 13–17: Highest Cash Dividend at 50%, One Major Bank to Pay Over VND 3,000 Billion
medium.summary:
Over 40 companies are scheduled to set dividend record dates during the week of July 13–17, with approximately 30 paying cash dividends ranging from 2% to 50%. Notably, BIDV (ticker: BID, HOSE) will set its record date on July 20 for a 4.5% cash dividend on FY2025 earnings, translating to VND 450 per share and a total payout of approximately VND 3,276 billion (~USD 130 million). The ex-dividend date is July 17, with payment expected August 20. Additionally, BIDV's board has approved a bonus share issuance of nearly 498.2 million shares (~6.84% of outstanding shares) from equity, expected in Q2–Q3 2026, which will further expand the bank's charter capital. For bond and FX investors, large dividend outflows from a systemically important bank like BIDV are worth monitoring as they represent meaningful liquidity movements within the banking sector. The capital raise via bonus shares also signals BIDV's intent to strengthen its capital adequacy ratios ahead of potential Basel III requirements.

---

medium.title: SJC Gold Bar and Plain Gold Ring Prices – Afternoon of July 11
medium.summary:
Gold prices in Vietnam remained elevated on July 11, with SJC gold bars quoted at VND 146.9–149.9 million/tael and plain gold rings at VND 146.6–149.6 million/tael. Bao Tin Manh Hai recorded a sharp upward price adjustment on July 10 and held those levels into the July 11 morning session. On international markets, spot gold was trading at approximately USD 4,119/oz, largely unchanged over the prior 24 hours. According to Kitco News, late Friday (US time) saw spot gold and silver edge lower as rising US Treasury yields and persistent expectations that the Fed will maintain elevated interest rates outweighed support from a weaker USD and escalating geopolitical concerns around the Strait of Hormuz. Market sentiment continues to be pulled in opposing directions following the June US jobs report and the FOMC meeting minutes released last Wednesday. **Relevance:** Domestic gold price dynamics relative to international benchmarks provide a secondary signal for VND purchasing power and informal FX pressure. The Fed's hawkish hold posture, reflected here, has direct implications for USD strength and therefore USD/VND trajectory. Traders should monitor whether widening domestic-international gold spreads prompt any SBV intervention signals.

---

medium.title: 20 Years of VSDC Development: Gradually Bringing Vietnam's Securities Market Closer to International Standards
medium.summary:
The Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation (VSDC) marked its 20th anniversary (2006–2026) at a ceremony attended by senior government and financial regulators, including the Deputy Minister of Finance, the State Securities Commission Chairwoman, and representatives from domestic and international financial institutions. The event reaffirmed VSDC's role as a critical market infrastructure institution underpinning the safe, transparent, and efficient operation of Vietnam's capital markets. This milestone is relevant in the context of Vietnam's imminent FTSE Russell emerging market upgrade, as post-trade infrastructure quality — including clearing, settlement, and depository functions — was a key criterion cited by FTSE Russell in its earlier review process. Continued investment in VSDC's systems signals ongoing commitment to meeting international standards that support greater foreign participation in Vietnamese equities and bonds.

---

medium.title: New Regulations on Average Retail Electricity Price Adjustments
medium.summary: On July 9, 2026, the Vietnamese government issued Decree No. 278/2026/NĐ-CP, amending certain provisions of Decree No. 72/2025/NĐ-CP, which governs the mechanism and timing for adjusting average retail electricity prices. Under the new rules, Vietnam Electricity Group (EVN) is required to calculate the average retail electricity price based on the power supply plan, production costs from year N-2, and estimated results for year N-1, submitting this by January 25 each year. **Relevance:** Electricity price adjustments are a direct upstream input into Vietnam's CPI basket. Any material increase in regulated electricity tariffs could add inflationary pressure, which the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) would need to factor into its monetary policy stance. For VND and bond traders, a significant tariff hike would be a watchpoint for inflation expectations and potential shifts in SBV's rate posture. Monitor the final tariff determination for FY2026.

medium.title: Which Countries Hold the Most Gold Reserves in the World?
medium.summary: Citing World Gold Council (WGC) data, central banks resumed gold purchases in May 2026, with Poland leading YTD acquisitions at 64 tonnes, followed by Uzbekistan (33t), China (25t), and Kazakhstan (20t). Singapore returned to net buyer status in May for the first time since September 2025, adding 4 tonnes. The US remains the world's largest holder at 8,133.5 tonnes. **Relevance:** While the article does not reference Vietnam's SBV gold reserve position directly, the broader trend of central bank gold accumulation — particularly among emerging market peers — is relevant context for Vietnam's own reserve management strategy. The SBV has historically used gold market conditions to manage domestic gold price spreads and FX reserve composition. Active EM central bank gold buying also supports gold prices globally, which has implications for Vietnam's domestic gold market dynamics and associated SBV intervention activity.

medium.title: Vietnam Surpasses China in Footwear Exports to the US
medium.summary: Vietnam's footwear exports reached USD 2.1 billion in May 2026, with cumulative 5-month exports totaling USD 9.78 billion (+0.18% YoY). Critically, exports to the US — Vietnam's largest footwear market — rose 5.94% YoY to USD 3.79 billion, representing 38.83% of total footwear export value, with Vietnam reportedly surpassing China in US market share for this category. The Netherlands and Belgium ranked second and third as destination markets. **Relevance:** Strong US-bound export performance is a positive signal for Vietnam's trade balance and current account surplus, both of which are key structural supports for the VND. Sustained export momentum reduces the current account vulnerability that could otherwise pressure the VND/USD exchange rate. For FX traders, robust export receipts support USD inflows and reduce SBV's need for FX intervention to defend the Dong. Watch for whether this trend sustains given ongoing US tariff policy uncertainty.

medium.title: Dragon Capital Names Three Stock Groups with Bright Prospects for H2 2026; One Group Expected to See 100% Profit Growth
medium.summary:
In its latest strategy report, Dragon Capital outlines three key drivers for Vietnamese equities in H2 2026: (1) accelerated public investment disbursement alongside supportive monetary and fiscal policy to meet growth targets; (2) Vietnam's official inclusion in the **FTSE Russell Secondary Emerging Market** index from **September 2026**; and (3) attractive market valuations that leave room for expansion if corporate earnings growth and liquidity align. Dragon Capital pegs the VN-Index's forward P/E for 2026 at approximately **11.7x**, which it characterizes as compelling. Excluding Vingroup-affiliated stocks (which account for ~29% of market cap but contribute disproportionately less to earnings), the broader market's valuation picture appears even more attractive. One sector is flagged with potential for **100% profit growth**. For international fund managers, the FTSE upgrade catalyst in September is the most actionable near-term event, as passive fund inflows tied to index rebalancing could provide a structural tailwind for VN-Index liquidity and foreign capital flows into Vietnamese equities. Watch for pre-inclusion positioning and any SBV FX intervention to manage USD demand from repatriating foreign investors.

---

medium.title: Vietcombank H1 2026 Business Results Update: Positive Figures Reported, While Sacombank's Profit Estimated to Have Halved
medium.summary:
Vietcombank reported strong H1 2026 results at its mid-year Party and Business Review Conference held on July 10, 2026. Total assets reached nearly VND 2.67 quadrillion (approximately USD 105 billion), up 9.83% from end-2025. Market 1 deposits exceeded VND 1.75 quadrillion, while credit outstanding hit VND 1.74 quadrillion, growing 4.8% YTD. FDI enterprise lending was a standout driver, growing over 16%, with SME lending up 10.4%. International payment and trade finance turnover rose 16.1%, reflecting Vietnam's continued role as a supply chain destination. In contrast, Sacombank's H1 2026 profit is estimated to have fallen by approximately 50%.

The Vietcombank data is directly relevant to capital flow dynamics — the strong FDI-linked credit growth confirms sustained foreign capital absorption in Vietnam's banking system, a positive signal for VND stability and current account support. Sacombank's sharp profit decline warrants monitoring for potential asset quality implications in the broader banking sector.

---
